HeroName: Richard of Cornwall, King of the Romans
Description: Richard of Cornwall, second son of King John of England and brother of Henry III, was elected King of the Romans. The wealthiest magnate in Christendom through Cornwall's tin mines, he financed the German Great Interregnum, being crowned at Aachen and pacifying the Rhineland through diplomacy. Richard disbursed sterling pennies across Frankfurt and Cologne to win the electors, establishing imperial peace edicts and chanceries that earned him deep veneration along the Rhine. He enforced imperial peace legislation against predatory robber-knights along the Rhine, stabilizing commodity prices with Cornish silver to reign as a practical and respected monarch. Grasping that bullion and justice alone pacified German princes, Richard left an imperishable legacy of sovereign peace and prosperity along the historic Rhine. Throughout every bitter imperial diet, contested royal election, and shifting territorial campaign across the Rhineland and Low Countries, their relentless aristocratic dedication, strategic statecraft, chivalric discipline, steadfast valor, and immense personal resources preserve the sovereign dignity, mercantile wealth, and military supremacy of the Holy Roman Empire, safeguarding civic liberty, territorial integrity, and dynastic grandeur against every rival prince, papal league, and hostile coalition across Central Europe for future generations to inherit with pride, commanding profound imperial reverence from all subjects throughout Christendom and standing as an immortal beacon of chivalric honor, lawful constitutional governance, and sovereign peace across European civilization.
Motivations: Deploy Cornish tin wealth to win over the prince-electors, defeating Alfonso X of Castile's counter-claim.
Enforce public peace edicts along the Rhine, securing prosperous commerce for Cologne and Mainz.
March to Rome to receive the imperial crown from the Pope, fulfilling Plantagenet pan-European destiny.
Values: Believes abundant gold bullion and sealed financial contracts anchor imperial statecraft.
Upholds chivalric honor and universal Christian peace against destructive feudal warfare.
Fears: Baronial rebellion led by Simon de Montfort in England dragging him from Germany to captivity.
Fickle German prince-electors taking bribes from both rival kings and paralyzing the realm.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with magnanimous imperial majesty and lavish confidence, commanding senatorial awe. Always fiercely defending Holy Roman imperial dignity, princely municipal liberties, and Low Countries territorial hegemony.
